proposals.before: second year of In of Kaihuang (582), with war planned against the south, he was appointed campaigning commander-in-chief of the Southeast Circuit, leading eight area commanders from Shouyang in a combined land-and-water advance.
proposals.after: In the second year of Kaihuang (582), with war planned against the south, he was appointed campaigning commander-in-chief of the Southeast Circuit, leading eight area commanders from Shouyang in a combined land-and-water advance.
proposals.reason: Corrupted opener 'second year of In of Kaihuang' omits 'In the' and invents 'In of'; Chinese is 開皇二年.

proposals.before: second year of In of Jiande (573) he was appointed magistrate of Cangcheng in Yong Prefecture, and soon afterward was transferred to magistrate of Dangyin.
proposals.after: In the second year of Jiande (573) he was appointed magistrate of Cangcheng in Yong Prefecture, and soon afterward was transferred to magistrate of Zhouzhi.
proposals.reason: Corrupted 'second year of In of Jiande' and 'Dangyin' misrender 建德二年 and 盩啡 (standard 盩厔/Zhouzhi).

proposals.before: In the second year of Jiande he was appointed Magistrate of Cangcheng in Yong Prefecture, and soon transferred to be Magistrate of Dangyin.
proposals.after: In the second year of Jiande he was appointed Magistrate of Cangcheng in Yong Prefecture, and soon transferred to be Magistrate of Zhouzhi.
proposals.reason: Literal 'Dangyin' does not match 盩啡令; the toponym is the known county 盩厔 (Zhouzhi), with 啡 a likely corruption of 厔.

proposals.before: When the Prince of Xiang was still in his fief, he was on friendly terms with Lan; after he took the throne his courtesy toward him increased, and Lan was promoted in one step to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
proposals.after: When Emperor Wu was still in his fief, he was on friendly terms with Lan; after he took the throne his courtesy toward him increased, and Lan was promoted in one step to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
proposals.reason: Chinese 武帝在籓 does not name a Prince of Xiang; the referent is Emperor Wu while still a prince in his fief.

proposals.before: Some years later he became Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and was advanced to General-in-Chief with the ceremonial equipage of the Three Excellencies.
proposals.after: Some years later he became Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and was advanced to kaifu yitong sansi (equal in ceremony to the Three Excellencies).
proposals.reason: 開府儀同三司 is a prestige rank with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies, not General-in-Chief.

proposals.before: Several years later he was transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and advanced in rank to General-in-Chief with the ceremonial equipage of the Three Excellencies.
proposals.after: Several years later he was transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and advanced in rank to kaifu yitong sansi (equal in ceremony to the Three Excellencies).
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 開府儀同三司 as General-in-Chief in the literal field.

proposals.before: first year of In of Daye (605) he was made Director of the Court of Judicial Review and again sent as commissioner on the Southwest Circuit to inspect local customs.
proposals.after: In the first year of Daye (605) he was made Director of the Court of Judicial Review and again sent as commissioner on the Southwest Circuit to inspect local customs.
proposals.reason: Corrupted opening omits In the and invents stray In of; Chinese is 大業元年.

proposals.before: At first he was not yet known, and people did not recognize his worth; only the High Ancestor, upon a single meeting, sighed deeply in wonder at him, took his hand, and said to those present, "Young Master Zhangsun's martial skill stands above the crowd; suited to his words, he also has many extraordinary stratagems.
proposals.after: At first he was not yet known, and people did not recognize his worth; only the High Ancestor, upon a single meeting, sighed deeply in wonder at him, took his hand, and said to those present, "Young Master Zhangsun's martial skill stands above the crowd; having spoken with him, one finds he also has many extraordinary stratagems.
proposals.reason: 適與其言 means after speaking with him, not suited to his words.

proposals.before: In the time of Emperor Xuan, the Türk qaghan Shetu requested marriage with Zhou; the daughter of Prince Zhao of Zhao was given to him in marriage.
proposals.after: In the time of Emperor Xuan, the Türk qaghan Shetu requested marriage with Zhou; the daughter of Zhao, Prince of Zhao, was given to him in marriage.
proposals.reason: 趙王招 is Prince of Zhao whose given name is Zhao; Prince Zhao of Zhao wrongly doubles the fief name.

proposals.before: first year of In of Kaihuang (581) Shetu said, "I am kin to the house of Zhou, yet now the Duke of Sui has seized power and I cannot stop him—how can I face the qaghan?"
proposals.after: In the first year of Kaihuang (581) Shetu said, "I am kin to the house of Zhou, yet now the Duke of Sui has seized power and I cannot stop him—how can I face the Kehedun?"
proposals.reason: Removes the corrupted 'In of' before Kaihuang; 可賀敦 is the khatun/consort (Kehedun), not the qaghan.

proposals.before: By the first year of Kaihuang, Shetu said, "I am kin to the house of Zhou; now the Duke of Sui has set himself up and I cannot restrain him—what face have I to show the qaghan?"
proposals.after: By the first year of Kaihuang, Shetu said, "I am kin to the house of Zhou; now the Duke of Sui has set himself up and I cannot restrain him—what face have I to show the Kehedun?"
proposals.reason: 可賀敦 denotes the qaghan's consort (Kehedun), not the qaghan himself.

proposals.before: He joined Gao Baoning in storming Lin Prefecture's Yu Pass and conspired with the tribal chiefs of the various departments for a joint southern invasion.
proposals.after: He joined Gao Baoning in storming the Linyu garrison and conspired with the tribal chiefs of the various departments for a joint southern invasion.
proposals.reason: 臨渝鎮 is the place-name Linyu garrison/pass, not 'Lin Prefecture's Yu Pass'.

proposals.before: He therefore joined Gao Baoning in attacking and capturing Lin Prefecture's Yu Pass, and arranged with the various tribal chiefs to plot a joint invasion southward.
proposals.after: He therefore joined Gao Baoning in attacking and capturing the Linyu garrison, and arranged with the various tribal chiefs to plot a joint invasion southward.
proposals.reason: 臨渝鎮 is Linyu garrison, not a Lin Prefecture Yu Pass.

proposals.before: Win over Chuluohou and connect him with the Xi and Mohe as well, and Shetu will have to split his forces to guard the east.
proposals.after: Win over Chuluohou and connect him with the Xi and Xí as well, and Shetu will have to split his forces to guard the east.
proposals.reason: 霫 is the Xí people, not the Mohe (靺鞨).

proposals.before: Again draw in Chuluohou and link him with the Xi and Mohe—then Shetu will divide his forces and return to guard the left.
proposals.after: Again draw in Chuluohou and link him with the Xi and Xí—then Shetu will divide his forces and return to guard the left.
proposals.reason: 霫 is Xí, not Mohe.

proposals.before: Sheng was made General of Chariots and Cavalry, marched out by the Yellow Dragon route, presented gifts to the Xi, Mohe, Khitan, and others, and used them as guides until he reached Chuluohou, won his confidence, and persuaded him to submit to the dynasty.
proposals.after: Sheng was made General of Chariots and Cavalry, marched out by the Yellow Dragon route, presented gifts to the Xi, Xí, Khitan, and others, and used them as guides until he reached Chuluohou, won his confidence, and persuaded him to submit to the dynasty.
proposals.reason: 霫 is Xí, not Mohe (靺鞨).

proposals.before: Sheng was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry, went out by the Yellow Dragon road, carried gifts to bestow upon the Xi, Mohe, Khitan, and others, and sent them as guides so that he reached Chuluohou's camp, laid his heart bare in depth, and induced him to submit inwardly.
proposals.after: Sheng was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry, went out by the Yellow Dragon road, carried gifts to bestow upon the Xi, Xí, Khitan, and others, and sent them as guides so that he reached Chuluohou's camp, laid his heart bare in depth, and induced him to submit inwardly.
proposals.reason: 霫 is Xí, not Mohe.

proposals.before: In the second year Shetu led four hundred thousand horsemen in from Lan Prefecture to Zhoupan, routed Chief of the West Daxi Changru's army, and prepared to drive farther south.
proposals.after: In the second year Shetu led four hundred thousand horsemen in from Lan Prefecture to Zhoupan, routed Daxi Changru's army, and prepared to drive farther south.
proposals.reason: Chinese 破達奚長儒軍 names only Daxi Changru; 'Chief of the West' is not in the source.

proposals.before: In the second year, Shetu with four hundred thousand horsemen entered from Lan Prefecture as far as Zhoupan, defeated the army of the Chief of the West, Daxi Changru, and wished to press farther south.
proposals.after: In the second year, Shetu with four hundred thousand horsemen entered from Lan Prefecture as far as Zhoupan, defeated the army of Daxi Changru, and wished to press farther south.
proposals.reason: Source has only 達奚長儒; 'Chief of the West' is an invented office.

proposals.before: Yuan Xie of Le'an said, "Let them behead him where he stands to punish his crimes."
proposals.after: Yuan Xie of Le'an West said, "Let them behead him where he stands to punish his crimes."
proposals.reason: Chinese reads 樂安西元諧; idiomatic English drops 西 from the place phrase.

proposals.before: The emperor was delighted, promoted him to General-in-Chief, and sent him back into the Türk lands to execute Princess Dayi.
proposals.after: The emperor was delighted, granted him the additional rank of Kaifu, and sent him back into the Türk lands to execute Princess Dayi.
proposals.reason: 開府 denotes the Kaifu privilege of establishing a headquarters, not General-in-Chief.

proposals.before: The emperor was greatly pleased, gave him the additional rank of General-in-Chief, and again sent him into the Türk domain to go and execute Princess Dayi.
proposals.after: The emperor was greatly pleased, gave him the additional rank of Kaifu, and again sent him into the Türk domain to go and execute Princess Dayi.
proposals.reason: 開府 denotes the Kaifu privilege of establishing a headquarters, not General-in-Chief.

proposals.before: Sheng was ordered to lead the surrendered Türks as campaigning commander-in-chief of the Qin River Circuit under Prince Guangs of Jin.
proposals.after: Sheng was ordered to lead the surrendered Türks as campaigning commander-in-chief of the Qin River Circuit under Prince Guang of Jin.
proposals.reason: English misspells the given name 廣 as "Guangs"; it should be "Guang".

proposals.before: first year of In of Renshou (601) Sheng memorialized, "I climbed the city tower at night and saw north of the desert a red mist more than a hundred li long, hanging to earth like bloody rain.
proposals.after: In the first year of Renshou (601) Sheng memorialized, "I climbed the city tower at night and saw north of the desert a red mist more than a hundred li long, hanging to earth like bloody rain.
proposals.reason: Corrupted opening inserts stray "In of" before Renshou; should read as the first year of Renshou.

proposals.before: Soon Rangan was invested as Qaghan Yili Zhen Douqi and given an archery contest in the Hall of Martial Peace.
proposals.after: Soon Rangan was invested as Qaghan Yili Zhendou Qiren and given an archery contest in the Hall of Martial Peace.
proposals.reason: English "Yili Zhen Douqi" fuses and drops 啟人 from 意利珍豆啟人可汗; the title should preserve Qiren.

proposals.before: third year of In of Daye (607) Emperor Yang visited Yulin, planned to march beyond the border in full array through the Türk lands toward Zhuo commandery.
proposals.after: In the third year of Daye (607), Emperor Yang visited Yulin and planned to march beyond the border in full array through the Türk lands toward Zhuo commandery.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English is corrupted (“In of Daye”) and lacks a grammatical connector; 大業三年 means the third year of Daye.

proposals.before: Rangan summoned the tribes under him; dozens of chieftains of the Xi, Mohe, Shiwei, and others assembled.
proposals.after: Rangan summoned the tribes under him; dozens of chieftains of the Xi, Xí, Shiwei, and others assembled.
proposals.reason: 霫 is the Xi/Xí people, not Mohe (靺鞨); the idiomatic English invents Mohe for 霫.

proposals.before: Rangan heard this and therefore summoned the tribes under him; several tens of chieftains of the Xi, Mohe, Shiwei, and other peoples all gathered.
proposals.after: Rangan heard this and therefore summoned the tribes under him; several tens of chieftains of the Xi, Xí, Shiwei, and other peoples all gathered.
proposals.reason: Same error as the idiomatic field: 霫 is not Mohe.

proposals.before: When Liang rebelled at Bing Prefecture, Xingbu held the city with Dou Lu Yu and others and resisted him; when the city fell he was killed.
proposals.after: When Liang rebelled at Bing Prefecture and led troops south against the imperial army, Xingbu was left to hold the city and, with Dou Lu Yu and others, shut the gates against Liang; when the city fell he was killed.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic version omits that Liang led forces south and that Xingbu was left for city defense, collapsing distinct Chinese clauses.

proposals.before: The historians comment: The Zhangsun clan, beloved since the northern frontier, came to establish ritual at Luoyang; their house bore noble emblems and bound itself to the realm.
proposals.after: The historians comment: The Zhangsun clan, from Daiyin, came to take their place with due ceremony at Luoyang; their house transmitted bells and cauldrons and swore upon mountains and rivers.
proposals.reason: 爰自代陰 names the place Daiyin; “beloved since the northern frontier” invents affection and erases the toponym.

proposals.before: The historians comment: The house of Zhangsun, from Daiyin in their affection, came to measure their ritual at Luoyang; their gates transmitted bells and cauldrons, their house swore upon mountains and rivers.
proposals.after: The historians comment: The house of Zhangsun, from Daiyin, came to take their place with due ceremony at Luoyang; their gates transmitted bells and cauldrons, their house swore upon mountains and rivers.
proposals.reason: “in their affection” is an unsupported reading of 爰自; 來儀 is ceremonial arrival, not “measure their ritual.”

decisions.reason: 開皇二年 is “In the second year of Kaihuang”; the before string’s stray “In of” is a real corruption, and the proposed opener restores grammatical English without changing sense.
建德二年 requires “In the second year of Jiande,” and 盩啡 is the transmitted glyph for the Yong-prefecture county 盩厔 (Zhouzhi), not Dangyin; the proposed idiomatic fixes both errors.

sourceWitness.citation: https://ctext.org/wiki.pl?chapter=269241&if=en (transmitted 盩啡; standard county 盩厔/Zhouzhi)
sourceWitness.excerpt: 建德二年，授雍州倉城令，尋轉盩啡令

decisions.reason: Literal “Dangyin” does not render 盩啡令; the office is magistrate of Zhouzhi (盩厔), with 啡 a corruption of 厔 in the transmitted digital text.

sourceWitness.citation: https://ctext.org/wiki.pl?chapter=269241&if=en (transmitted 盩啡; standard county 盩厔/Zhouzhi)

decisions.reason: 武帝在籓 names Emperor Wu while still in his fief; “Prince of Xiang” is invented and unsupported.
開府儀同三司 is the prestige rank kaifu yitong sansi (ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies), not “General-in-Chief.”
Same mistranslation in the literal field: 開府儀同三司 is not General-in-Chief.
大業元年 is “In the first year of Daye”; the corrupted “In of Daye” opener is a real error.
適與其言 means after speaking with him / in conversation with him, not “suited to his words.”

decisions.after: In the time of Emperor Xuan, the Türk qaghan Shetu requested a marriage alliance with Zhou; the daughter of Yuwen Zhao, Prince of Zhao, was given to him in marriage.
decisions.reason: 趙王招 is Yuwen Zhao, Prince of Zhao. The original wrongly made Zhao part of the title, while the proposal remained needlessly ambiguous by omitting his compound surname.

decisions.after: In the first year of Kaihuang (581), Shetu said, "I am kin to the house of Zhou, yet now the Duke of Sui has seized power and I cannot stop him; how can I face the khatun?"
decisions.reason: The corrupted Kaihuang opener needs repair, and 可賀敦 means the khatun, not the qaghan. The standard English title is clearer here than a transcription of the Chinese transcription Kehedun.

decisions.after: By the first year of Kaihuang, Shetu said, "I am kin to the house of Zhou; now the Duke of Sui has set himself up and I cannot restrain him; what face have I to show the khatun?"
decisions.reason: 可賀敦 denotes the qaghan's consort, or khatun, not the qaghan. The standard English title is clearer than Kehedun.
臨渝鎮 is the place-name Linyu garrison, not “Lin Prefecture’s Yu Pass.”
Same place-name error in the literal: 臨渝鎮 is Linyu garrison.
奚、霫 are the Xi and Xí peoples; 霫 is not Mohe (靺鞨).
Literal likewise misrenders 霫 as Mohe; Xí is correct.
Again 奚、霫、契丹; Mohe invents a different people for 霫.
Same Mohe error in the literal field for 霫.
破達奚長儒軍 names only Daxi Changru; “Chief of the West” is not in the Chinese.
Literal invents the same unsupported office “Chief of the West” for 達奚長儒.

decisions.after: Yuan Xie, Duke of Le'an, said, "Let them behead him where he stands to punish his crimes."
decisions.reason: The dossier’s 樂安西元諧 is a corrupt/variant reading; CText and parallel editions have 樂安公元諧 (Yuan Xie, Duke of Le'an). The proposal’s “Le'an West” invents a false place from 西, while the before text already omitted the real title 公.
加授開府 grants the Kaifu privilege, not promotion to General-in-Chief.
Literal likewise misrenders 開府 as General-in-Chief; Kaifu is correct.
晉王廣 is Prince Guang of Jin; “Guangs” is a misspelling of 廣.
仁壽元年 is “In the first year of Renshou”; the stray “In of” is a real corruption.
意利珍豆啟人可汗 must preserve 啟人 (Qiren); “Yili Zhen Douqi” fuses the title and drops that element.
大業三年 is “In the third year of Daye”; the proposed sentence also restores a grammatical link after Yulin.
奚、霫、室韋 again pairs Xi with Xí; Mohe is not in the source.
Literal Mohe for 霫 is the same invention; Xí is correct.

decisions.after: When Liang rebelled at Bing Prefecture and led troops south against the imperial army, Xingbu was left to hold the city and, with Doulu Yu and others, shut the gates against Liang; when the city fell he was killed.
decisions.reason: The original collapses 率眾南拒官軍 and 乃留行布城守. The revision restores Liang's southward march and Xingbu being left to defend the city, and correctly treats 豆盧 as Doulu Yu's compound surname.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 率眾南拒官軍，乃留行布城守，遂與豆盧毓等閉門拒諒

decisions.after: The historians comment: The Zhangsun clan came from Daiyin to grace the capital at Luoyang. For generations their lineage enjoyed the honors of high office, and their house held fiefs pledged to endure as long as the mountains and rivers.
decisions.reason: 爰自代陰 names Daiyin, while 門傳鍾鼎 and 家誓山河 praise hereditary high office and enduring enfeoffment. The revision conveys those allusions in natural English instead of reproducing their ritual objects literally.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 長孫氏爰自代陰，來儀京洛，門傳鍾鼎，家誓山河

decisions.after: The historians comment: The house of Zhangsun came from Daiyin and made its ceremonial appearance at the capital of Luoyang; at their gates bells and cauldrons were handed down, and their house swore by the mountains and rivers.
decisions.reason: The literal field should preserve the imagery while removing the unsupported 'in their affection' and the mistranslation of 來儀 as 'measure their ritual.'

claimRetractions.reason: Revised r0020 shows 樂安公 is Yuan Xie’s noble title (Duke of Le'an), not a native-place formula; the native-place claim was created only by reading 樂安 as origin.

claimAdditions.reason: Standard text 樂安公元諧 identifies Yuan Xie by the dukedom of Le'an; that title should replace the retracted native-place reading.
